title: Common Do-Calculus Derivations across Families of Causal Graphs
banked_reason: Sound positive-binary Der_C separation, but D0.5.G graded it subfield below the fixed field floor (paper_score_ceiling 6.5 < 7.4; salvageable=false).
gap_reasons: The delivered result proves a nontrivial positive-binary separation for the explicitly defined domain-typed grammar Der_C; it does not prove that Yvernes et al.'s informal ICD language is extensionally equivalent to Der_C, so the advertised hierarchy correction remains conditional.

Observed-variable minimality is confined to binary, strictly positive, unconditional atomic queries, while graph-count minimality is proved only under permissive compatibility and not for the genuine-edge exact class.

These scope restrictions and the absence of a demonstrated consequence for identification practice constrain its significance and projected leading-econometrics-journal score despite the field-level proof-theoretic contribution.
proof_attempt_summary: The run constructed and independently checked a strictly positive binary counterexample: a shared adjustment functional for two DAGs, a transfer obstruction through a nonidentifying ADMG, observationally colliding SCM witnesses, and scoped variable/graph minimality results. The mathematics and citations passed D0.5 after correcting the prior-art positioning, but the result applies to the paper's explicit Der_C grammar rather than a proved formalization of the source's informal ICD language. A future re-raise would need an independently justified formal proof language and a proved inclusion connecting every anchor-admissible derivation to the transfer-safe calculus; this run must not assume that correspondence.
tldr: In the strictly positive binary specialization of the common-identification framework of Yvernes et al., one observational functional need not admit one family-common finite proof: the two DAGs \(G_1\) and \(G_2\) share \(F(P;x,y)=\sum_zP(y\mid x,z)P(z)\), but every common typed do-calculus derivation transfers to an ADMG with observationally identical positive SCMs having different effects. Three observed variables are minimal under both permissive and genuine-edge exact-positive compatibility. Two graphs are also minimal under permissive compatibility, by fixed-graph completeness plus a separately proved typed compilation lemma; no graph-count claim is made for the exact class.
gap: Fixed-graph completeness proves graphwise proof existence, whereas common derivability requires one proof whose every graphical leaf is valid throughout a family. The literature explicitly leaves whether common-functional identification can exceed this common proof notion unresolved, and no cited result covers arbitrary finite families with full domain-typed probability algebra.
fill: Formalize the family-indexed proof language, prove equality-and-domain transfer, certify the twelve shared schemas, verify the corrected rational collision and exact latent projection, prove the scoped two-variable lower bound using \(Der_{C_prime}\), and state uniform compilation as a proof-carrying definition with its immediate corollary.
